summary: Hexaware's quarter revenue was $411.9 million, up 1.6% sequentially and 4.3% year on year.
Revenue came in below management's expectations, mainly due to a softer GSE client and delayed large deals.
Adjusted EBIT margin was 13.8% after 160 bps of one-off items; full-year adjusted margin narrowed to 13-13.5%.
Management gave no formal guidance this quarter and said Q4 will likely dip seasonally, as in past years.
Headcount rose to 35,887; IT attrition was stable at 11.1%.

story.what_it_does: Hexaware is an IT services company that earned about USD 1,537 Mn in revenue in CY25, with roughly 33,800 staff at year-end. It serves large clients, with the top 10 making up 36.4% of revenue, and says it launches one new service every month.
story.plans: Management guided CY26 EBIT margin to 13-14% and wants to move 70% of campus electricity to renewables and raise women to 40% of staff by 2030. In the latest quarter it planned a Netherlands restructuring, a strategy review within 90 days, and 1,000 Anthropic-certified staff and AI architects by the middle of next year.
story.moat: The notes do not describe a clear moat. Some stability shows in IT attrition near 11% and a client base that is becoming less concentrated, with the top 5 at 24.7% of revenue versus 26.0% a year earlier. The company itself flags AI as a risk that could cut the effort and revenue in existing services.

scenarios.story: Delayed large deals start ramping and growth picks up, as constant-currency growth did in Q2 CY26 at 6.3%. Margins improve through the year and the Netherlands restructuring lifts operating margins.
signals_to_watch: Constant-currency revenue growth returning above the 6.3% seen in Q2 CY26
Adjusted EBIT margin staying in or above the 13-13.5% range

scenarios.story: Growth stays modest at about 4-5% year on year, with margins near the low end of the 13-14% guide and a seasonal dip in Q4. A new leadership team reviews strategy and forecasting.
signals_to_watch: Outlook given with full-year results after no Q4 guidance
